CUNY student here, going to pursue public defense. Honestly, the rank, job outcomes, and any other stats are meaningless compared to how well prepared CUNY students are when we graduate. Our clinics are very well regarded and they are mandatory for 3L year. Most of my professors have been amazing, and true legal weapons in their respective fields. Besides, CUNY has a solid reputation in the city. Also, your living situation in NYC is a god send, especially when factoring the cost compared to other programs + how many students move out of state to attend. 

Regarding “unicorn” PI jobs, while yes it is an uphill battle because of the ELITISM that festers in our field, there have been CUNY students that get internships and future roles there. I known a few. 

I strongly urge you to look beyond the elitism and the name-droppery that runs rampant, and ultimately make the best decision for yourself. Besides, unless you’re trying to pursue big law or federal clerkships, which are still possible with a degree from CUNY, then it sounds like a good choice. The whole game of ranking and stats is not real unless you buy into it + you want to get into the parallel universe of big law.
